duplicate-5c64a44b95ee5656.hint: Which energy-transfer route is excluded by “adiabatic”? Apply the first law with that term removed.
notes: Adiabatic means Q = 0, so ΔU = −W when W is work done by the gas. Expansion can cool the gas; compression can warm it.

ibd-a570e27c0010b5b2-q7:a.iv.text: The heat input is approximately 416 J and the heat rejected is approximately 332 J. The net work is 416 − 332 = 84 J. Therefore η = W/Qin = 84/416 ≈ 0.20, or 20%.

ibd-a570e27c0010b5b2-q7:b.text: The entropy is greatest at B. During the isothermal expansion A → B the gas absorbs heat, increasing its entropy. Cooling B → C reduces its entropy. The reversible adiabatic path C → A has no entropy change, so SA = SC < SB.

fep-6d03205b0ef8f56e-qC1:b.vi.text: The turbine supplies mechanical power 600/0.75 = 800 MW. Its thermal efficiency is 800/2400 = 1/3. For the ideal Carnot limit, η = 1 − Tc/Th. Thus Th = 300/(1 − 1/3) = 450 K.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:a.text: Draw an arrow Qin from the hot reservoir into the engine, an arrow W from the engine to useful work, and an arrow Qout from the engine to the cold reservoir. Label Qin = W + Qout; if arrow widths represent energy, the input width equals the sum of the two output widths.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.i.text: D → A is the isothermal compression: volume decreases along the lower-temperature isotherm.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.ii.text: C → D is the adiabatic expansion: volume increases without heat transfer, and the gas cools.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.iii.text: Work is done on the gas during D → A and A → B. Both are compression stages, so the volume decreases.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:b.iv.text: Heat enters during B → C and leaves during D → A. The other two stages are adiabatic and have no heat transfer.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:c.text: The area enclosed by the cycle on the pressure–volume diagram is the net work delivered in one cycle. The clockwise direction corresponds to positive net work done by the gas.

fep-03ac6c29c12025a9-qC2:d.text: With the same hot-reservoir temperature, a colder outdoor reservoir in winter reduces Tc/Th. The maximum efficiency η = 1 − Tc/Th therefore increases. Both temperatures must be in kelvin.

fep-7149c2746ea8ea6f-qC1:a.text: AB is isothermal. At A, pV = (2.0 × 10⁵)(5.0 × 10⁻³) = 1000 J; at B, pV = (5.0 × 10⁵)(2.0 × 10⁻³) = 1000 J. For a fixed amount of ideal gas, equal pV means equal temperature. The steeper curve AC is the adiabatic compression.

fep-7149c2746ea8ea6f-qC1:c.text: Estimate the area between AC and AB over the compression from 5.0 × 10⁻³ to 2.0 × 10⁻³ m³. The work done on the gas is greater along AC by approximately 1.6 × 10² J. A small grid square represents (0.1 × 10⁵ Pa)(0.1 × 10⁻³ m³) = 1 J, so counting the enclosed squares gives the estimate.

fep-7149c2746ea8ea6f-qC1:d.text: For the adiabatic compression, Q = 0. Work done on the gas increases its internal energy. Since the internal energy of a fixed amount of ideal gas depends on temperature, its temperature rises.
